# MakeHardware — network access for the cloud environment
#
# This choice decides what the toolchain can do. Pick one of the three below.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OPTION A — Custom, minimum viable (recommended starting point)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Set Network access to **Custom**, TICK "Also include default list of common
# package managers", and paste these two lines:

ppa.launchpadcontent.net
*.frame.claudeusercontent.com

#   ppa.launchpadcontent.net
#     KiCad 10 packages. Launchpad serves PPA content from this host. The
#     Trusted preset lists only launchpad.net and the RETIRED ppa.launchpad.net
#     (which no longer connects at all). Without this line apt-get update only
#     warns, still exits 0, and apt-get install kicad silently gives you KiCad
#     7.0.11 from Ubuntu universe — which has no IPC API, so Konnect cannot
#     drive it.
#
#   *.frame.claudeusercontent.com
#     Lets Claude read back the vision boards and reports it publishes as
#     Artifacts.
#
# What you still cannot do on Option A: install LTspice, fetch datasheets from
# vendor sites, or call a paid image-generation API.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OPTION B — Custom, plus the vendor sites you actually use
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Everything in Option A, plus whichever of these matter to you. Add vendor
# domains as you hit them; the agent will tell you which host it was denied.

# ltspice.analog.com        # LTspice installer      (also set MH_ENABLE_LTSPICE=1)
# *.analog.com              # ADI datasheets and models
# *.ti.com                  # TI datasheets and app notes
# *.microchip.com           # Microchip datasheets
# ww1.microchip.com
# *.st.com                  # ST datasheets
# *.nxp.com
# *.digikey.com             # parametric search and stock
# *.mouser.com
# *.snapeda.com             # symbols and footprints
# *.samacsys.com
# fal.run                   # paid image generation, if you outgrow HF Spaces
# *.fal.ai
# api.bfl.ai

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OPTION C — Full network access
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No allowlist at all; any domain is reachable. Worth considering for this
# workflow specifically, because sourcing and documentation both mean fetching
# from arbitrary vendor sites you cannot predict in advance — with an
# allowlist, every new manufacturer is a config change before the agent can
# read its datasheet.
#
# The trade is that a session can reach anywhere, so treat any credential you
# put in the environment as exposed to whatever the agent reads. If that is
# acceptable for this work, Option C removes a whole category of friction.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Already covered by "Also include default list of common package managers":
# pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, index.crates.io, static.crates.io,
# static.rust-lang.org, github.com, codeload.github.com, archive.ubuntu.com,
# security.ubuntu.com, *.ubuntu.com (which covers keyserver.ubuntu.com, where
# the KiCad PPA signing key comes from).
#
# NOT affected by any of this — these are properties of the base image and the
# GitHub proxy, and hold at every network level including Full:
#   * add-apt-repository is broken (python3 is 3.11, python3-apt ships 3.12)
#   * protobuf-compiler alone cannot build Konnect; libprotobuf-dev is required
#   * GitHub release assets 403 for repos not attached to the session, so
#     Konnect must be built from source no matter how open the network is
#   * the ~5 minute setup budget, 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM / 30 GB disk
